Prerequisite: A zero trust network access (ZTNA) or endpoint protection platform (EPP) license applied to EMS for each managed endpoint (EPP includes every ZTNA feature)
What it enables: Endpoint registration (if no ZTNA license is applied, no endpoint can register to EMS), Fabric Agent telemetry, security posture tagging, the Dynamic Security Fabric connector, remote access (IPsec VPN and SSL VPN), Vulnerability Scan, and ZTNA
How to put it in place: Buy the licenses (at least 25 endpoints), register them in FortiCloud with the EMS hardware ID, and log EMS in to FortiCloud; GUI: Dashboard > Status (License Information, License Source: FortiCare)
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "License types" (Windows, macOS, and Linux licenses, and the EPP and ZTNA feature comparison) and "Licensing FortiClient"

Prerequisite: An EPP license for the endpoints that use the EPP-only features
What it enables: Antivirus, anti-ransomware, anti-exploit, cloud-based malware detection, the Application Firewall, software inventory, USB device control, the FortiClient Outbreak Detection service (FortiGuard outbreak alert rules), and FortiClient Cloud Sandbox (SaaS)
How to put it in place: Buy EPP licenses for those endpoints (EMS applies licenses by the features enabled in each endpoint's profile); GUI: Dashboard > Status (License Information)
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "License types" (EPP and the EPP and ZTNA feature comparison) and "FortiGuard Outbreak Alerts" (with an EPP license)

Prerequisite: A supported EMS host or platform: Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 LTS, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 with an active Red Hat subscription, or CentOS Stream 9 (Windows Server for EMS 7.0 and 7.2), with at least 6 virtual CPUs, 12 GB RAM, and 80 GB free disk, no other installed services, and not a domain controller; or a virtualization platform for the EMS VM image, or Docker Compose or Kubernetes
What it enables: Installing EMS (FIPS mode is chosen at installation) and assessing the host against its operating system STIG
How to put it in place: Build the host to the System requirements and the Management capacity sizing, then install EMS on it; emscli system get info
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "System requirements", "Management capacity", and "Installation parameters" (enable_fips); FortiClient EMS 7.0.0 Administration Guide (Windows Server)

Prerequisite: Internet access from the EMS host during installation and upgrades: the Linux distribution, PostgreSQL, and other package repositories, and FortiCloud (or, in an air-gapped network, the dependencies bundle or an HTTP proxy)
What it enables: EMS installation and upgrades, the automatic upgrade to the latest patch release, and the upgrade notifications, which EMS gets by checking FortiCloud for the latest patch release
How to put it in place: Allow outbound access to the destinations listed for EMS installation and upgrade in Required services and ports, at least during upgrade windows; emscli system set proxy
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "System requirements" (an active internet connection), "Required services and ports" (EMS installation and upgrade), and "Automatically upgrading EMS to latest patch release" (internet access is required); FortiClient & FortiClient EMS 7.4 New Features Guide, "Deploying EMS in air-gapped environments"

Prerequisite: Access from EMS to the FortiGuard servers (or a FortiManager that serves FortiClient software and signatures)
What it enables: Antivirus and vulnerability signature and engine updates, FortiClient installer creation and downloads, the FortiGuard outbreak alert rules, and the EMS and FortiClient upgrade and compatibility matrix signature
How to put it in place: Allow outbound TCP 80, or TCP 443 for FortiGuard Anycast, to the FortiGuard servers and TCP 443 to forticlient-rs.forticloud.com; GUI: System Settings > FortiGuard Services (Enable SSL, Use FortiManager for client software/signature updates)
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "Required services and ports" (FortiGuard, EMS installer creation) and "Configuring FortiGuard Services settings"; FortiClient & FortiClient EMS 7.4 New Features Guide, "FortiClient and EMS upgrade and compatibility matrix signature"

Prerequisite: DoD-approved network time (NTP) servers configured as the time source of the EMS host
What it enables: Accurate time stamps on EMS logs, alerts, and events
How to put it in place: Point the time service of the EMS host at the NTP servers (an operating system setting); emscli execute time
Source: FortiClient EMS 8.0.0 CLI Reference, "emscli execute time" (synch synchronizes the host time with the network time)

Prerequisite: A DNS name (FQDN) for EMS and server certificates for it from a DoD-approved CA for the web server (GUI, installer downloads, and websocket) and endpoint control services
What it enables: Browser trust of the EMS console, and FortiClient validation of the EMS certificate (name match, a CA trusted by the endpoint operating system, not expired), so that the invalid certificate action can be set to deny
How to put it in place: Add the DNS record and request the certificates for the EMS FQDN; GUI: System Settings > EMS Server Certificates
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "EMS Server Certificates" and "Adding an SSL certificate to FortiClient EMS"; FortiClient 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Endpoint communication security"

Prerequisite: The DoD PKI root and intermediate CA certificates (the issuing CA chain of each server certificate that EMS or FortiClient validates)
What it enables: FortiClient validation of the VPN gateway certificate, the CA certificates that EMS installs on endpoints, and EMS validation of the LDAPS directory and SMTP server certificates
How to put it in place: Download the CA certificates from the DoD PKI and install them in the EMS host certificate store; GUI: Endpoint Policy & Components > CA Certificates
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "CA Certificates", "Adding an ADDS server" (Certificate for the LDAPS connection), and "Configuring SMTP Server settings" (the CA must be in the certificate store of the EMS host)

Prerequisite: A code signing certificate from a DoD-approved CA, with its password, and a timestamp server
What it enables: Signing of the Windows FortiClient installers that EMS creates or receives
How to put it in place: GUI: System Settings > EMS Settings (Sign Software Packages, Timestamp server, Certificate)
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "Configuring EMS settings" (Sign Software Packages, Timestamp server, Certificate, Password)

Prerequisite: A custom intermediate CA certificate and private key (PEM or PKCS12) from the organization's PKI, and FortiOS 7.6.3 or later on the FortiGates
What it enables: EMS signing the FortiClient ZTNA certificates with your own CA instead of its default ZTNA root CA
How to put it in place: Issue the intermediate CA certificate and key from the organization's PKI, and upgrade the FortiGates to FortiOS 7.6.3 or later
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "Uploading custom certificate and private key for ZTNA"

Prerequisite: A remote backup server reachable over SCP or SFTP (or FTP from emscli), with a user that has write access to the target location
What it enables: EMS database backups stored on another system
How to put it in place: Create the backup account and directory on the server; GUI: System Settings > EMS Settings (Backup Server: Remote)
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "Configuring EMS settings" (Scheduled Backup, Backup Server); FortiClient EMS 8.0.0 CLI Reference, "emscli execute backup" (copy service and remote user)

Prerequisite: A second EMS VM (and, from 7.4.6, witness database nodes) on a virtualization platform, deployed as a new 7.4.5 or later EMS VM HA deployment, with hostnames set
What it enables: The EMS VM HA cluster, in which the secondary nodes sync to the PostgreSQL database of the primary node
How to put it in place: Deploy the VMs, set their hostnames, and join them to the primary node with the EMS VM ha commands; emscli system set hostname; emscli ha get nodes
Source: FortiClient & FortiClient EMS 7.4 New Features Guide, "Creating an EMS VM HA cluster using the EMSCLI" and "Adding witness nodes to EMS VM HA clusters"

Prerequisite: An Elasticsearch cluster running Elasticsearch 8.14.0 or later, with an API key for EMS (and its CA certificate when the cluster checks client certificates)
What it enables: The Endpoints > All Events page (consolidated endpoint events) on on-premises EMS
How to put it in place: Install EMS with the Elasticsearch parameters (elastic_api_key, elastic_ca_path), or enable the integration after installation
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "All Events", "Installing EMS with ES integration", and "Enabling ES integration after EMS install"

Prerequisite: An SMTP server that accepts mail from EMS over SMTPS or STARTTLS, with a certificate from a CA in the certificate store of the EMS host
What it enables: EMS alerts and endpoint alerts by email
How to put it in place: GUI: System Settings > SMTP Server (Server, Security: SMTPS, Send Test Email)
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "Configuring EMS Alerts", "Configuring Endpoint Alerts", and "Configuring SMTP Server settings"

Prerequisite: A FortiAnalyzer (or FortiAnalyzer Cloud) that accepts logs from the endpoints and from EMS, with EMS added as an authorized device; or a syslog server for FortiClient logs
What it enables: Off-loading of FortiClient logs and Windows host events, and of EMS system logs
How to put it in place: In FortiAnalyzer, add EMS in Device Manager with the EMS serial number; for syslog, set up a syslog server that the endpoints can reach
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "Sending EMS system log messages to FortiAnalyzer" and "Relationship between FortiClient EMS, FortiGate, and FortiClient" (FortiClient sends logs and Windows host events to FortiAnalyzer); FortiClient 8.0.0 XML Reference (log_protocol syslog, netlog_server)

Prerequisite: An Active Directory domain (AD DS) reachable over LDAPS with a server certificate, a bind account for the read-only connection, and DNS resolution of the domain for Kerberos
What it enables: Directory administrators and AD groups assigned to admin roles, AD endpoint and user import, AD group tagging rules, the AD connector, and user verification with an LDAP server
How to put it in place: GUI: Administration > Authentication Servers (LDAPS connection, Certificate hostname check)
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "Adding an ADDS server", "AD connector", "Required services and ports" (Active Directory server connection), and "Configuring user verification with an LDAP server for authentication"

Prerequisite: A Microsoft Entra ID tenant with EMS or the FortiGate registered as an application (Entra ID-joined endpoints for seamless autoconnect, and Windows Hello for Business for its logon)
What it enables: The Entra ID authentication server, user verification with Entra ID, VPN autoconnect with the Entra ID logon, and Windows Hello for Business with FortiGate SAML-based IPsec VPN
How to put it in place: Register the application in Entra ID; GUI: Administration > Authentication Servers
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "Adding an Entra ID server", "Configuring user verification with Entra ID authentication", and "Autoconnect on logging in as an Entra ID user"; FortiClient & FortiClient EMS 7.4 New Features Guide, "Windows Hello Business support for FortiGate SAML-based IPsec VPN"

Prerequisite: A SAML identity provider (FortiAuthenticator, FortiGate, Entra ID, Okta, or AD FS), preferably one that enforces CAC
What it enables: SAML SSO for EMS administrators, SCIM provisioning from the identity provider, user verification with SAML, and SAML authentication for VPN with the FortiGate as the service provider
How to put it in place: GUI: Administration > SAML SSO
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "SAML SSO" (FortiGate, Okta, Entra ID, AD FS, and FortiAuthenticator as IdP), "Adding a SCIM server", and the user verification sections; FortiClient 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "SAML support for VPN"

Prerequisite: A RADIUS server with EMS as a client (shared secret) and PAP, CHAP, or EAP-MD5
What it enables: RADIUS logon for EMS administrators
How to put it in place: GUI: Administration > RADIUS (Client Secret, Test Connection)
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "RADIUS"

Prerequisite: A FortiGate connected to EMS through the FortiClient EMS Fabric connector and authorized in EMS (FortiOS 6.2.0 or later for dynamic endpoint groups, 7.0.0 or later for the ZTNA device certificate)
What it enables: Sharing of endpoint information and security posture tags with FortiGate, FortiGate validation of the EMS-issued ZTNA certificates, distribution of the FortiGate SSL deep inspection CA certificates, and the per-VDOM and token-authenticated Fabric connections
How to put it in place: Add the FortiClient EMS Fabric connector on the FortiGate (a FortiOS setting); GUI: Fabric & Connectors > Fabric Devices
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "Relationship between FortiClient EMS, FortiGate, and FortiClient" and "Fabric Devices"

Prerequisite: A FortiGate IPsec VPN gateway (IKEv2; FortiClient 8.0.0 supports only IKEv2) or SSL VPN gateway configured to match the Remote Access profile, with a server certificate from a DoD-approved CA
What it enables: Every provisioned VPN tunnel, and the gateway side of full tunneling, SAML, FortiToken Mobile push, and the EMS serial number check (vpn-ems-sn-check)
How to put it in place: Configure the VPN gateway on the FortiGate (FortiOS settings)
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Configuring an IPsec VPN connection" (only IKEv2), "SAML support for VPN", and "Connecting VPN with FortiToken Mobile"; FortiClient & FortiClient EMS 7.2 New Features Guide (vpn-ems-sn-check in the FortiOS global settings)

Prerequisite: A FortiGate ZTNA access proxy (ZTNA server and ZTNA rules) for the ZTNA destinations, on FortiOS 7.0.0 or later
What it enables: ZTNA TCP forwarding and HTTPS access through the FortiGate with the device certificate that FortiClient receives from EMS
How to put it in place: Configure the ZTNA server and rules on the FortiGate (FortiOS settings)
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "Relationship between FortiClient EMS, FortiGate, and FortiClient" (FortiClient 7.0.0 and FortiOS 7.0.0 or later)

Prerequisite: FortiToken Mobile on the users' Android or iOS devices, with tokens and push notification configured on the FortiGate
What it enables: IPsec VPN with FortiToken Mobile push MFA
How to put it in place: Assign FortiToken Mobile tokens to the VPN users on the FortiGate and enable push
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Connecting VPN with FortiToken Mobile"

Prerequisite: CAC smart cards with user certificates from the DoD PKI, and smart card readers on the endpoints (FortiClient (Linux) does not support smart cards; FortiClient finds the certificate only for the user who was logged on when the card was inserted)
What it enables: Smart card certificate authentication for VPN
How to put it in place: Issue the CACs and install the card readers on the endpoints
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "Access to certificates in Windows Certificates Stores" and "FortiClient feature comparison"

Prerequisite: An endpoint operating system on which FortiClient supports the module: Vulnerability Scan on Windows, Windows Server, macOS, and Linux (not iOS or Android); ZTNA TCP forwarding on the desktop platforms, while iOS and Android support only the ZTNA HTTPS proxy with the ZTNA certificate pushed through an MDM; smart card authentication not on Linux
What it enables: The module on that endpoint; an endpoint on an unsupported platform does not get the setting
How to put it in place: Check the FortiClient feature comparison for each endpoint platform; for mobile ZTNA, set up the MDM integration; GUI: System Settings > MDM Integration
Source: FortiClient 8.0.0 Administration Guide, "FortiClient feature comparison"; FortiClient 8.0.0 EMS Administration Guide, "Deploying ZTNA certificates to FortiClient mobile via MDM"
